newsitem.title: UK: London gold opens year with fix at four-week low.
newsitem.headline: London gold opens year with fix at four-week low.

text.p: Gold was fixed at its lowest level since December 3, 1996 at its first fixing of 1997 on Thursday, reflecting the impact of late selling in New York on Tuesday.
Bullion fixed at $367.80 per ounce after $369.55 at its pre-holiday fixing on Tuesday morning.
"It is not trying too hard to move far away from $368 this morning. I think people will wait to see what direction comes from Comex," one dealer said.
The February Comex futures contract ended down $2.00 at $369.20 on Tuesday, with most of the selling coming in the closing minutes of the session.
Some dealers questioned whether the move represented a serious retrenchment for the gold price or was a continuation of year-end position squaring.
"It may be a bear trap," one dealer said.
Another issue which caused caution about gold's weak start to the new year was platinum extending its premium over gold, having been flat to discounted in the final weeks of 1996.
"You can't see gold turning round while platinum is at a discount. Now that platinum is back above it, that is another reason for doubting how far gold will fall," a dealer said.
Even so, the outlook for gold was still largely bearish. "A gold clear-out would be good for gold. I can see it down to $330-$340 in the early part of this year," one dealer said.
Business was pretty thin, with Tokyo closed overnight for a national holiday and the banks in Zurich also shut.

While platinum and silver were marginally below Tuesday's levels, palladium bucked the trend by fixing at its highest level since September 19, 1996 at $120.75, up from $116.50 at its previous fixing.

Dealers said palladium attracted buying on the Nymex futures market on Tuesday when the March contract closed up $5.25 at $124.25. They added that compared with weak gold and platinum, palladium had been steady through the closing weeks of 1996.

Concerns about the continuing availability of Russian exports and steady substitution of palladium in many applications for its more expensive sister metal platinum were behind the move in New York, dealers said.
Platinum was indicated at $369.50/$370.50, down about 50 cents from Tuesday's level, while silver attracted little interest at $4.77/$4.79, off a couple of cents.
